StackType.rationale: PowerStackType.Counter. The sim has no StackType concept; Power.on_stack adds unconditionally, which is what PowerCmd.ModifyAmount does (PowerCmd.cs:236 -- no StackType branch). Third-file citations, not hashed here.

AfterAttack.issue: RE-VERIFIED 2026-07-30, residual unchanged, enumeration re-executed against today's tree. THE HOOK IS FIXED: SuckPower implements `after_attack(dealer, card, results)` (powers.py:1951-1965), the sim's Hook.AfterAttack bracket, and `hooks.after_attack` hands it the (receiver, unblocked) pairs DamageCmd.deal accumulates. It counts the connecting hits (`receiver.side != self.owner.side and unblocked > 0`) and applies `self.amount * hits` ONCE after the attack, so the mid-attack self-boost and the killing-blow skip are both gone. WHAT REMAINS: SuckPower.cs:23's third early-return condition, `!command.DamageProps.IsPoweredAttack()`, is still not expressed anywhere -- the sim's `after_attack` bracket carries no `props` argument at all and powers.py:1958 tests only the dealer identity and the receiver's side. DORMANT, enumerated: SuckPower's only ported applier is `FossilStalker` (monsters/underdocks/fossil_stalker.py:38-40, `PowerCmd.apply(hooks, self, SuckPower, _SUCK_STR)` on itself), an enemy, and every one of its three moves (`_tackle`, `_latch`, `_lash`) routes damage through `Monster._execute_attack` (monsters/base.py:127-138), which calls `DamageCmd.deal(ctx.hooks, ctx.player, damage, dealer=self)` with NEITHER `card` NOR `props` supplied -- `DamageCmd.deal`'s own default-inference (cmds.py:201-205) then sets `props = DamageProps.CARD` (== MONSTER_MOVE, powered) whenever both are omitted. EXECUTED (`grep -rn "props=" sts2_rl/monsters/`): the one hit anywhere under monsters/ is `BlockCmd.apply(..., props=ValueProp.UNPOWERED)` in glory/fabricator.py -- a BLOCK grant, not damage, and not inside an attack bracket -- so no ported monster ever deals unpowered damage inside a before_attack/after_attack bracket. Named trigger, unchanged: any unpowered damage dealt inside an attack bracket by a Suck owner (none ported). This record's group-counting guard is untouched and still open.

guards.what: SuckPower.cs:32-36 the pet de-duplication (RemoveAll on the pet owner's results)
guards.rationale: Pets/Osty belong to the other characters; in Ironclad scope each hit group has one receiver and the de-duplication is a no-op.

guards.what: Counting GROUPS with unblocked damage, not individual results
guards.issue: RE-VERIFIED 2026-07-30. C#'s `num` counts outer lists (per-hit result groups) in which ANY result had unblocked damage, so a single AoE hit that connects with three creatures counts 1. The sim's `after_attack` counts every connecting (receiver, unblocked) pair as its own hit (powers.py:1960-1961, `hits = sum(1 for receiver, unblocked in results if ...)`), so the same AoE would grant 3x instead of 1x. Folded into the hook entry's rollup; carried separately because it survives an after_attack-slot fix. DORMANT, enumerated: SuckPower's only ported applier is Fossil Stalker (monsters/underdocks/fossil_stalker.py, read in full), whose three moves -- TACKLE (`_tackle`), LATCH (`_latch`) and LASH (`_lash`, 2 hits) -- all call `self._execute_attack(ctx, damage, hits)`, which loops `DamageCmd.deal(ctx.hooks, ctx.player, damage, dealer=self)` calling the SINGLE `ctx.player` once per hit (monsters/base.py:134-135) -- never more than one receiver per hit, and the sim's combat scope is single-player throughout (Ironclad only), so there is no content-reachable way to produce a `results` list with more than one receiver in one hit. Named trigger unchanged: any AoE monster move with a Suck owner (none ported; would additionally require a multi-target combat shape the sim does not have).
